newsitem.title: USA: Excite aims to boost ad rates with channels.
newsitem.headline: Excite aims to boost ad rates with channels.

text.p: Excite Inc. CEO George Bell said the Internet search company hopes to generate higher advertising base rates through the channel strategy which it will implement in a week's time.

Excite earlier posted a first quarter loss of $8.8 million, or $0.72 a share, compared with a $5.6 million, or $0.50 a share, loss in the year-earlier period. The latest loss was $3.9 million less than in the fourth quarter of 1996 and included a total of $4.3 million of merger and acquisition-related costs.
Revenues gained 15 percent sequentially to $7.5 million in the first quarer from $6.5 million in the December quarter, and were up five-fold from $1.4 million a year ago.

Bell said the quarter did not include significant revenues from its AOL NetFind search and directory service co-branded with America Online Inc, which was launched at the end of the quarter and which has been logging up to 4 million pages a day.
The company also did not benefit from a full quarter of selling advertising space on WebCrawler, which it acquired from America Online late last year.
Without the one-time charges, Excite's pro-forma per-share loss would have been $4.5 million, or $0.37 a share, better than analyst's consensus estimates of a loss of $0.43.
All but one of the four public search and navigation companies -- including Lycos Inc and Infoseek Corp continue to report losses.

Yahoo Inc has been the only company to begin posting a modest profit, doing so last week for the second straight quarter. Infoseek is expected to post a modest loss when it reports earnings on Thursday.

Excite has been the major acquirer in the rapid consolidation of the Internet search engine business, with two major acquisitions last year, seeking to build market share by acquisition to be able to compete for market leadership. "I

think the market share game is pretty clear right now," Bell told Reuters in an interview, noting that Excite's rate of roughly 18 million pages a day is second only to Yahoo Inc, which reported an average of 30 million in March.

But the next competitor is likely posting half of the number of pages a day, he said, while PC Meter in February ranked Excite's sites, including WebCrawler and Excite, as having the largest unduplicated reach of all, at 43 percent.

Bell said Excite, which in March filed to sell up to 2.3 million common shares in the first secondary offering by one of the search companies, was taking a "wait and see" posture towards the market, which has recently been volatile.
"I think it's a very tough market," he said.
Excite shares were off 1/2 at 11-1/2.
Bell said the number of advertisers at Excite was up significantly to more than 430. "The number of non-technology advertisers is 44 percent of that number," he said.

The company has shrunk the amount of barter in its business to 18 percent including its deal with Netscape Communications Corp, from 23 percent in the fourth quarter," he said. Non-Netscape barter was six percent in the quarter.
Bell said the company is seeing longer-term contracts among the middle-level advertisers willing to shell out around $250,000 to $500,000 on an annualized basis.
But major advertising spenders were still underspending on a relative basis, he added.

Bell said that by launching a set of topic-based channels next week, Excite hopes to attract advertisers to pay higher rates. Currently, Excite can average around $18 on a cost per thousand (CPM) page views basis, and he said it hopes to attract CPMs of $35 to $40.
"It gives us a chance to create inventory in the place where it's desired," he said of the channels, noting it can run specific finance, sports, entertainment or computing channels.
((sam.perry@reuters.com, Palo Alto Bureau 415 846 5400))
